diagram_classification: computistical / calendrical (probably a twelve-part wheel of the months or of the zodiac, with a possible cosmological reading)
interpretation: A wheel-shaped schema with a large green outer rim, a small inner hub ring and twelve spokes. The twelve-fold division most plausibly stands for the twelve months of the year (or the twelve zodiacal signs or twelve winds), with the rim as the enclosing cycle of the year and the hub as the centre of the cycle. The spokes are coloured in alternating green, ochre and pink tones, which suggests a grouping, perhaps by seasons or by the four elements, though the grouping is not certain. The diagram is unlabelled in its visible parts. The outer circle is the annual circuit, the spokes divide it into equal parts, and the hub is the fixed centre, perhaps the earth or a place for a title or a number. The ghost text visible behind it is show-through from the other side of the leaf and is not part of the diagram. The specific content (months, signs, winds or something else) is uninterpreted because no inscriptions are legible.
evidence: Visible: a circle with a thick green rim, a concentric central ring in pink and ochre, and twelve radial bands in alternating green, ochre and pink with curved joins at the rim and the hub. The twelve equal divisions and the wheel form are the grounds for a calendrical or zodiacal reading. External: medieval computistical manuscripts commonly use twelve-part wheels for the months, zodiac signs or winds. No labels or figures are legible, so the exact subject cannot be confirmed. The text showing through the parchment is not part of the diagram.
